about: Where each muscle of the anatomy atlas arises and inserts, as the textbooks give it, and the atlas structures expected at each end. Read by tools/anatomy_attach_audit.py (which checks each muscle's ends against it) and tools/anatomy_attach.py (which moves an end onto its landmark). The textbook statements are written fresh from the sources cited (Gray's Anatomy, 1918, public domain; OpenStax Anatomy and Physiology 2e, CC BY 4.0); Kenhub and Netter were only looked at.

sources.title: Anatomy of the Human Body (Gray's Anatomy), 20th edition
sources.author: Henry Gray, revised by Warren H. Lewis
sources.note: Sections and pages are the 1918 edition's; plates are its figure numbers (Wikimedia Commons keeps them as File:Gray<n>.png, public domain).

sources.title: Anatomy and Physiology 2e
sources.author: J. Gordon Betts et al.
sources.note: Sections and figure numbers are the 2e's.

how.match: a regular expression on the structure's node name; a row covers both sides unless sided is false
how.bones: keys of bone_keys: each key's expression per body names the atlas structures ({S} is the muscle's own side, L or R; {side} the same as left or right; a key with no structure in a body, such as the woman's hyoid, leaves that end unchecked there)
how.kind: end: a tendon or narrow end, checked where it meets the bone; area: a broad fleshy attachment, checked along the deep face; soft: on a soft structure, listed only
how.find: how the audit finds the end on the mesh: cap [x, y, z] is the share of the muscle's points farthest along that direction (x lateral for a muscle of one side, the body's left for one of the midline; y up; z forward); far [x, y, z] is the end of the muscle's longest way along its surface lying farther that way; face [u0, u1] is its deep face, the points facing the expected bones within reach metres, between those shares of its length from origin (0) to insertion (1)
how.moved_by: a tool that makes the muscle to measure and owns its shape: tools/anatomy_attach.py leaves it alone
how.layer: the order tools/anatomy_attach.py moves muscles in: the deeper first (0, the default), a muscle over them after (the gluteus minimus 1, medius 2, maximus 3); each gives way to those moved before it
how.keep_side: metres: an end whose muscle must lie in front of its first landmark's patch of bone: tools/anatomy_attach.py brings the points straight behind it by that much or less (in the bone, or through a thin one: the iliacus and the iliac wing) back in front, the muscle moving with them
how.midline: metres: tools/anatomy_attach.py keeps the muscle at least this far from the body's midline on its own side (the midline as the suite finds it: the middle of the sacrum's width over its lower half)
how.to: how tools/anatomy_attach.py moves a wrong end: to its first landmark the tools find (the default), or nearest, onto the nearest part of its bones (a broad end whose landmarks are reported only)
how.verdicts: OK: on the right bone within 2 mm; FLOATING: the right bone nearest, farther than 2 mm; WRONG BONE: another bone nearest; INSIDE BONE: the end more than 2 mm inside a bone; UNKNOWN: no row
how.new rows: a muscle added to the atlas needs a row: its match, its kind, origin and insertion with bone keys (add a key if its bone has none) and a find, and its cite and images

femur.greater_trochanter.lateral.what: the lateral surface of the greater trochanter (its oblique ridge)
femur.greater_trochanter.lateral.found: femur points lateral to the head centre by 3 cm or more, 4 to 28 mm below the trochanter's top, facing out (normal's lateral share over 0.55)

femur.greater_trochanter.anterior.what: the anterior border and surface of the greater trochanter
femur.greater_trochanter.anterior.found: the same band of the trochanter, facing forward (normal's forward share over 0.5)

femur.lesser_trochanter.what: the lesser trochanter (its tip and the bone just below it)
femur.lesser_trochanter.found: the femur's point farthest back and in from the shaft's axis, 35 to 95 mm below the head's centre, and the bone within 9 mm of it

femur.gluteal_tuberosity.what: the gluteal tuberosity, on the back of the upper shaft
femur.gluteal_tuberosity.found: not found by the tools yet

ilium.aiis.what: the anterior inferior iliac spine and the bone within 8 mm of it
ilium.aiis.found: the ilium's most forward point 12 to 50 mm above the acetabulum's centre (the femoral head's), within 45 mm of it across

ilium.supra_acetabular.what: the groove above the rim of the acetabulum
ilium.supra_acetabular.found: hip bone points 20 to 32 mm from the head's centre, above it, facing up or out

ilium.gluteal_surface.what: the outer (gluteal) surface of the ilium's wing
ilium.gluteal_surface.found: ilium points above the acetabulum's centre, facing out or back (normal's lateral share over 0.3)

ilium.iliac_fossa.what: the iliac fossa, the inner face of the ilium's wing
ilium.iliac_fossa.found: ilium points 15 mm or more above the acetabulum's centre, facing in and forward (normal's medial share over 0.3, up to the crest)

ilium.iliac_crest.posterior.what: the posterior part of the iliac crest and the posterior superior iliac spine
ilium.iliac_crest.posterior.found: ilium points within 40 mm of its most backward point above the acetabulum

patella.base.what: the base (upper border) of the patella
patella.base.found: the top fifth of the patella's height

vertebrae.T12_body.what: the side of the body of the twelfth thoracic vertebra, its lower half (the psoas's highest slip arises there and from the T12/L1 disc)
vertebrae.T12_body.found: the vertebra's points in front of its middle, facing out (normal's lateral share over 0.3), below their middle height

sacrum.dorsal_surface.what: the dorsal surface of the sacrum (its median and lateral crests)
sacrum.dorsal_surface.found: sacrum points facing back (normal's backward share over 0.5)

muscles.name: gluteus maximus

origin.text: hip bone: the outer surface of the ilium behind the posterior gluteal line, and the posterior part of the iliac crest
sacrum: the back of its lower part and its side; the coccyx's side; the aponeurosis of the erector spinae and the sacrotuberous ligament
origin.note: its fibres on the sacrotuberous ligament and the erector spinae's aponeurosis (neither in the atlas) are not checked

insertion.text: femur: the gluteal tuberosity (its deep lower fibres); the rest into the iliotibial tract of the fascia lata (not in the atlas)

cite.section: IV. Myology: The Muscles and Fasciae of the Thigh (the gluteal region)
11.6 Appendicular Muscles of the Pelvic Girdle and Lower Limbs

muscles.name: deep back muscles (erector spinae and transversospinales)

origin.text: sacrum: its dorsal surface (median and lateral crests), the posterior part of the iliac crest, and the lumbar spinous processes, through the erector spinae's aponeurosis; the multifidus in the sacral gutter
along the column: the laminae, transverse and spinous processes of every vertebra it passes (the transversospinales between them), the angles of the ribs (iliocostalis)

insertion.text: the cervical vertebrae's transverse and spinous processes (iliocostalis, longissimus and semispinalis cervicis, multifidus); higher slips go on to the mastoid process and the occipital bone (longissimus and semispinalis capitis), beyond the atlas's segmented muscle
